questions.q: What punctuation mark must always be used to show that a character is speaking?
questions.a: Quotation marks (also called speech marks or inverted commas: " "). A wrong answer (like using only commas or dashes) suggests the student does not know how to distinguish between narration and actual speech.

questions.q: Why is dialogue between two characters who do not understand each other often considered "humorous"?
questions.a: It is humorous because the audience knows the truth while the characters stay confused, creating a funny gap in logic. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks humor is only about telling jokes, rather than situational comedy.

questions.q: Convert this sentence into direct dialogue: "Rahul told his sister that he had eaten the last mango."
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify the speaker (Rahul). 2. Identify the listener (his sister). 3. Identify the message (I ate the last mango). 4. Format: Rahul said, "I ate the last mango." A wrong answer shows the student is struggling with the transition from indirect to direct speech.

questions.q: If a character in a story is very serious, how can you use dialogue to make the scene humorous?
questions.a: Place the serious character in a silly situation where they try to use complex language to solve a simple, ridiculous problem. A wrong answer suggests the student assumes humor only comes from silly characters, missing the "clash of personalities" technique.

questions.q: Critique this dialogue: Character A says "Hello." Character B says "Hi." Why does this fail to "move the story forward"?
questions.a: It fails because it contains no new information, conflict, or character development; it is just a greeting. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks any exchange of words counts as "storytelling."

questions.q: Write a two-line dialogue where one character thinks they are at a train station but the other knows they are actually in a library.
questions.a: Criteria: The dialogue must clearly show the location confusion (e.g., "Why is the train so quiet?" vs "Sir, this is a library!"). A poor answer fails to show the specific misunderstanding.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Dialogue writing is the art of recording the exact spoken words between two or more characters, while humorous writing uses wit, surprises, or funny situations to make a story ______.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever tried to tell a ______ a funny story that happened at home, but forgot to say exactly what your mother said?
What is Dialogue writing? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Dialogue writing is the art of recording the exact spoken words between two or more characters, while humorous writing uses wit, surprises, or funny situations to make a story entertaining.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Dialogue writing?
questions.a: Students often think dialogue needs to be a "transcript" of every word said in real life, including "um," "ah," and boring greetings.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can write a 5-sentence conversation that includes a humorous element (like a misunderstanding) and punctuates the speech correctly using quotation marks.
